Time and memory by modeling task

Colocad 0.1.0-alpha.10, CadQuery 2.8.0 and build123d 0.13.0. On the 12 common scaling points, Colocad had the lowest median peak memory in 11/12 and the shortest median wall time in 6/12. These counts give each tested size one vote and are not a distribution of real projects.

One 100-second queue of full hand assemblies

Each job starts a new process. The same ordered edits change guide diameter and cable radius. Count only complete, independently reopened 43-solid STEP handoffs by the deadline. Memory is the largest 25 ms sample, not a per-job kernel peak. One window per backend.

All 23 comparable tasks

Cold process with warmed host caches. Scored fixtures: 512 MiB; scaling matrix: 2 GiB; both 1 vCPU, no swap/network. Scored fixture lanes share a host with pinned stress controls. Wall times include startup, native checks and export; inference, installation, independent OCCT readback and rendering are outside timing. Values are medians (min–max); a dash means no measurement. Lower retained output is not a measure of API flexibility.

Logical writes come from Linux /proc/PID/io at process exit including waited-for children. Retained files include Colocad checkpoints but exclude instrumentation and supplied inputs. Warm-cache block counters on a host bind mount cannot establish physical SSD bandwidth. All three tools are tested on real edits; there is no claim of universal CAD API parity.

Hybrid modeling in a 512 MiB sandbox

One fresh Linux process per case, including mixed STEP, GLB and offline HTML export. Memory includes charged file cache. These two builds use Colocad’s local hybrid executor.
